text:
lin: Heads-up — I posted the split-orchestrator RFC in docs: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/console-policy-orch. TL;DR: extract policy evaluation out of the query edge into a thin orchestrator service + lightweight edge guards. Looking for migration/playbook ideas.

sachin: see it, reading. main worry is p99 latency; adding a hop might break our 150ms SLO for interactive dashboards. Have numbers? :thinking_face:

lin: good call. initial perf model: orchestrator eval + async cache priming should add ~5–10ms median, p99 impact depends on cache hit. If we keep edge guards for hot prefixes (hybrid mode) p99 stays within target.

evie: correctness side: we can't accept even tiny windows where the orchestrator and edge disagree on policies. How do we handle policy updates and immediate revocation?

ryan: two thoughts: (1) strong invalidate path: orchestrator pushes invalidation to edge via delta stream (kafka) and edges subscribe; (2) fallback policy: if edge sees mismatch, use fail-open for read-only dashboards and fail-closed for write actions. We'll need product sign-off on behavioral changes.

lin: agreed on both. proposal sketch:

````
# config for hybrid rollout
policy_orchestrator:
  mode: hybrid     # hybrid | orchestrator-only | edge-only
  cache_ttl_ms: 120000
  invalidation_topic: console.policy.invalidations
  canary_percentage: 5
````

lin: invalidations are ordered by sequence id; edges apply idempotently. For immediate revokes we send a force-expire event that bypasses TTL.

sachin: ok, but streaming adds complexity. What's the failure mode if kafka lags? edges will serve stale decisions unless force-expire delivered — how long do we tolerate that?

evie: product asked for near-real-time revocation (<=5s) for sensitive actions. We need an SLA on invalidation delivery. Could we also have a direct push path for high-priority revokes?

ryan: we can implement a fast lane: orchestrator hits a push API on edges for priority keys (webhook over internal mesh). Fallback to stream if push fails. Push should be rate-limited and auth'd.

lin: rollout plan I want to propose:
- Step 0: feature flag only — no traffic. smoke tests.
- Step 1: canary at 5% traffic in orchestrator-only mode for non-sensitive read routes. monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
- Step 2: enable hybrid mode for canary, so edges still short-circuit hot paths.
- Step 3: expand to 25% with hybrid + invalidation stream. enable force-expire plugin and measure invalidation latencies.
- Step 4: production ramp with staged migration of write routes with fail-closed policy and product sign-off.

lin: monitoring we need:
- decision path histogram (edge vs orchestrator)
- token cost per decision (to check perf impact)
- invalidation tail latency (99/999)
- user-visible auth errors broken down by policy version

ryan: also add a canary test that flips a policy and asserts revocation within 5s. automation should run during ramp.

evie: for migration ops checklist:
- run policy diff tool to ensure parity between replicated rule sets
- enable debug logging for first 24h and sample decisions at 1% to verify audit trail
- fallback runbook: if orchestrator causes >2x p99 increase, rollback to edge-only flag and purge canary configs

sachin: small nit: sampling 1% debug logs will still be a lot. make sure we have retention and scrubbing — PII.

lin: yep, we'll sample decision context minus PII fields. security audit required before step 3.

deploy-bot: canary cluster created: orch-canary-5pct (id: canary-2026-03-21-01) — good luck :rocket:

ryan: perf test plan: synthetic QPS spike at canary, vary sequence length, measure cpu on orchestrator and net RTT. If CPU > 70% we either increase pool or switch to hybrid for that tenant.

evie: also add a migration window for enterprise tenants who want longer lead time — document a two-week opt-in path.

lin: thanks all. I'll draft the cutover doc and a short playbook for on-call and post it here. if anyone wants to pair on the canary automation, ping me. :+1:
